domain: volatility-shape and cross-sectional risk-state information from daily OHLCV (assigned A4 column)

mechanism.causal_economic_mechanism: Cross-sectional pricing of the SHAPE of sector risk, not its level or its trend. For each sector ETF, decompose trailing total variance into downside versus total second moment (semivariance share S = downside sum-of-squared-returns / total sum-of-squared-returns over the trailing 126 sessions). Three mutually reinforcing strands of the asset-pricing literature locate a premium in this shape statistic at the single-asset level: (a) the downside-risk strand (Ang-Chen-Xing) finds that assets whose returns co-vary more with the market when the market falls - i.e., downside-heavy assets - command higher subsequent returns as compensation for their asymmetric marginal contribution to downside; (b) the conditional-skewness strand (Harvey-Siddique) finds negative systematic skewness is priced with a positive premium; (c) the lottery-demand strand (Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw MAX effect) finds upside-heavy, lottery-like return distributions are systematically overpriced by demand and underperform. All three strands imply the same tradable direction in sector space: downside-heavy sectors (high S) are cheap relative to upside-heavy sectors (low S), so a market-neutral spread long high-S and short low-S should earn a positive expectancy. The sector-ETF level is a genuine out-of-sample transfer test: whether a demand/compensation effect documented within stocks survives aggregation to 11 large, liquid, institutionally-held sector composites is exactly the open, falsifiable question.
mechanism.why_after_cost_information_should_surviv: The arm is a market-neutral spread (gross <= 2.0, net ~ 0) whose leg membership changes only on discrete state transitions of a 126-session second-moment statistic, enforced by a hysteresis automaton with a monthly (21-session) decision clock and static weights between clocks. The state variable is persistent, so turnover is small (estimated 1.5-3.0 two-way per year, ~25-50% of the frozen 6.0 ceiling), giving an expected cost drag of only ~15-30 bps/year at the 10 bps base and ~30-60 bps at the 20 bps stress. Documented single-name spreads for this mechanism class are of order 1-3% per year; even if aggregation to sector composites halves the effect, the residual clears the cost drag. Because the book is net ~0 and market-direction exposure is removed both by construction and again by the frozen risk-matched SPY-context subtraction, any surviving expectancy is not SPY/sector beta and is not 'long when trend up': the signal is built exclusively from squared returns and a sign indicator, invariant to the direction of past returns.
mechanism.falsifiable_prediction: Directional and specific: the anchor spread (long the 4 highest semivariance-share sectors, short the 4 lowest, market-neutral, hysteresis book, monthly clock) has strictly positive expectancy after 10 bps/side base costs, positive incremental alpha versus the risk-matched SPY context overall, and risk-matched excess return in at least 2 of 3 folds. If the spread expectancy is positive but is reproduced by the level-sort control at ratio >= 0.5 (mechanism is variance LEVEL, not shape), or if the stable sign is opposite to the prediction, the anchor is rejected as specified - no post-hoc sign rescue.

primary_sources: Ang, Chen & Xing (2006), 'Downside Risk', Review of Financial Studies 19(4): 1191-1239 - downside-risk compensation; high downside-risk assets earn higher subsequent returns
Harvey & Siddique (2000), 'Conditional Skewness in Asset Pricing Tests', Journal of Finance 55(3): 1263-1295 - negative systematic skewness commands a positive risk premium

Bali, Cakici & Whitelaw (2011), 'Maxing Out: Stocks as Lotteries and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns', Journal of Financial Economics 99(2): 427-446 - upside-heavy (lottery-like) distributions are overpriced and underperform, implying the same long-downside-heavy direction

fields_used: for each of the 11 sector ETFs (XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY): {SYM}_all_p1.json values[].datetime and values[].close (split+dividend adjusted) - sole signal and return input; daily total returns are close-to-close on the adjusted path
SPY_all_p1.json values[].datetime and values[].close (adjusted) - benchmark context, risk-match scaling regression, and session calendar only; SPY is never a held leg

EW_SECTOR_TOTAL_RETURN equal-weight sector context derived from the same 11 {SYM}_all adjusted-close series per p2_a3_benchmark_contract.json membership and daily-rebalanced convention - used only in the sector-factor neutralization step
authorized_pit_inputs.fields_not_used: open, high, low, volume; the _none raw series (no price-level features are used, so the raw-path authorization is not exercised); distributions.json and split_factors.json evidence files (S0 scoring needs no manual corporate-action splicing on the _all path); no fundamentals, earnings, borrow, short-interest, holdings, flows, options or intraday fields (all unavailable per data manifest)
authorized_pit_inputs.window_discipline: S0 screening/scoring window 2018-04-04..2025-07-31; the 126-session signal window at the first S0 decision is filled from the authorized pre-S0 runway (2010-01-04..2018-04-03, 2076 sessions) exactly as provided for warmup; no scored computation reads any session after 2025-07-31

universe_and_schedule.universe: all 11 SPDR sector ETFs of the frozen cohort (XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY) - fixed non-cherry-picked rule: the full sector side of the frozen cohort, SPY excluded from legs because the frozen benchmark contract reserves it as market context; a sector enters the ranking only when it has >= 126 sessions of authorized adjusted-close history (XLC from ~126 sessions after its 2018-06-19 inception; before that it is excluded from ranks and held FLAT - an availability rule, not a selection)
universe_and_schedule.warmup_sessions: 126 sessions (well inside the 252-session allowance); filled from authorized pre-S0 history so the first S0 session (2018-04-04) is already a valid decision tick
universe_and_schedule.decision_clock: every 21st SPY session (session-count clock, no calendar dependence); signals computed on session-t close data, PIT; the automaton re-seeds with the seed rule on the first tick of each S0 fold (force-flat boundaries respected)
universe_and_schedule.holding_period: 21 sessions (one clock period); weights held static between decision ticks; no intraperiod rebalancing
universe_and_schedule.fill_clock: next allowed session per baseline invariants (t+1 open-adjacent, close-to-close execution consistent with ADJ-1-EXEC-CLOCK; never a same-session fill)

anchor: ANCHOR SFV4-A4-H1-ANCHOR, exact rule (no parameter menu): (1) Returns r_{i,s} from adjusted closes of sector i on SPY-calendar sessions. (2) At each decision tick t, for each eligible sector: SS_i = sum of r_{i,s}^2 over the trailing 126 sessions ending at t; DS_i = same restricted to sessions with r < 0; semivariance share S_i(t) = DS_i / SS_i. Rank eligible sectors by S_i descending (rank 1 = most downside-heavy); ties broken lexicographically by symbol. (3) Hysteresis book automaton over states LONG/SHORT/FLAT, evaluated only at ticks: seed (first tick of a fold): LONG := ranks 1-4, SHORT := ranks 8-11, others FLAT. Subsequent ticks, transitions applied in this fixed order: (i) exits - a LONG whose new rank >= 8 leaves LONG (to SHORT if |SHORT| < 4, else FLAT); a SHORT whose new rank <= 4 leaves SHORT (to LONG if |LONG| < 4, else FLAT); (ii) entries - FLAT sectors with rank <= 4 enter LONG in ascending-rank order while |LONG| < 4; FLAT sectors with rank >= 8 enter SHORT in descending-rank order while |SHORT| < 4; ties lexicographic. (4) Weights: +0.25 per LONG leg, -0.25 per SHORT leg; CASH absorbs the net residual; gross <= 2.0, net ~ 0; weights static between ticks. This is the single primary arm; the rank-4/4, band <=4/>=8, 126-session, 21-session-clock and 0.25 constants are fixed ex ante with no alternatives offered.
neighbour: SFV4-A4-H1-NEIGH, one fixed variant supporting the same mechanism: identical to the anchor in every element (4/4 hysteresis book, weights, clock, fill, universe, eligibility) except the state window is 63 sessions instead of 126. Mechanism-support logic: the downside-shape premium is a property of the risk state, not of one particular window length; if the mechanism is real, the shorter-window neighbour carries the same sign with positive expectancy, and agreement of both arms supports the mechanism while disagreement marks the anchor as window-specific. No other variant is proposed.

causal_negative_control.control: SFV4-A4-H1-CTRL, total-variance LEVEL sort: identical surface form to the anchor (same 126-session window, same rank-and-hysteresis 4/4 book, same weights, clock, fills, universe, eligibility, sector-factor neutralization) but sectors are ranked by SS_i (total sum of squared returns, i.e., variance level) descending; LONG := ranks 1-4 (highest variance), SHORT := ranks 8-11 (lowest variance). If the causal story is true - that the priced object is the COMPOSITION of sector variance (downside vs upside) and not its LEVEL - then after market neutralization and sector-factor removal a level-sort spread must NOT carry the premium: a high-vol-minus-low-vol sector spread is an unhedged risk-level bet with no documented directional premium once market/sector exposure is removed, and the lottery/downside strands are shape statements, not level statements.
causal_negative_control.preregistered_falsification_rule: The anchor passes only if |control risk-matched incremental alpha| < 0.5 x anchor risk-matched incremental alpha AND control expectancy <= 0. If control expectancy > 0 or the ratio reaches 0.5 (frozen gate control_alpha_abs_ratio_lt = 0.5), the spread is attributed to a variance-level effect rather than the claimed shape mechanism and the anchor is rejected; no alternate control may be substituted after results are seen.

factor_alpha_test.risk_matched_incremental_alpha: Per the frozen benchmark contract: incremental_alpha(arm, window) = R_arm(window) - R_spy_context(window), with R_spy_context = SPY total return scaled EX ANTE by the arm's frozen scaling rule, never realized gross re-applied after the fact. This arm's frozen scaling rule (declared here, market-neutral book): kappa_t = clip(beta_hat_t, 0.0, 2.0), where beta_hat_t is the OLS slope of the arm's spread daily returns (a deterministic function of the frozen rule, hence PIT-computable at t) on SPY total-return daily returns over the trailing 252 sessions ending t-1. Evaluated per fold and overall; gates per frozen stage-A: anchor overall alpha > 0 and risk-matched excess positive folds >= 2.
factor_alpha_test.sector_factor_neutralization: Sector beta is plausible (all legs are sector ETFs), so the required neutralization step is added: OLS of the arm's daily returns on [SPY total return, EW_SECTOR total return] over each fold and over all of S0; the intercepts are reported annualized alongside the risk-matched context metric. A result whose intercept after both-factor removal is not positive fails the mechanism claim regardless of raw PnL.
factor_alpha_test.fail_closed: raw PnL, gross beta or long-equity exposure is never accepted as alpha; all gates fail closed per baseline invariants

costs_and_turnover.cost_model: 10 bps per side per fill at base, 20 bps per side at stress, charged exactly once per fill per baseline invariants
costs_and_turnover.expected_turnover: weights are static between monthly ticks and the 126-session semivariance share is a persistent state statistic, so leg changes occur only on band-crossing transitions. Expected 1-3 swap events per side per year, each moving 0.25-0.75 of |delta w|: expected annualized two-way turnover ~1.5-3.0 (point estimate ~2.2), i.e., ~25-50% of the frozen 6.0 two-way/year ceiling. Cost drag ~22 bps/year at base, ~44 bps at stress. Two forced-flat fold-boundary events per cycle add negligible turnover.
costs_and_turnover.why_inside_ceiling: the design spends turnover only on genuine state transitions, which is exactly the trade content of the mechanism; hysteresis bands plus a slow-moving second-moment state plus static weights between monthly clocks structurally cap churn far below the ceiling with headroom for stress and boundary flattening

sample_size_floor.floors: >= 5 decisions/fold and >= 30 total are satisfied with large margin even if early-tick eligibility thinning or boundary realignment removes several ticks; at least 6-8 non-CASH legs are occupied at every tick, satisfying the min-positions invariant

drop_one_design.expected_max_concentration: 8 legs across 11 sectors with equal weights; ex ante no single sector should dominate spread contributions, but the honest hazard is a persistent pair-level relation (e.g., one energy- or utility-heavy episode) pushing one ETF's positive contribution above the frozen etf_positive_share_le = 0.35 gate; this is treated as a live hazard, not assumed away
drop_one_design.drop_one_etf: value_book rerun excluding the max-contribution symbol per frozen convention; survival = after-drop expectancy > 0; meaningful because the claim is a cross-sectional premium - it must not be a single-pair artifact
drop_one_design.drop_one_fold: min over folds of expectancy with that fold removed; survival = min > 0; meaningful because state-driven premia can be single-regime artifacts (e.g., only the 2020 crash episode), and the mechanism claims a persistent state premium, not one regime

failure_interpretation: A Stage-A reject means the downside-vs-total composition of sector variance carries no exploitable after-cost, market-neutral cross-sectional premium in large liquid sector ETFs: either the downside-risk/skewness/lottery-demand mechanisms do not transfer from single stocks to sector composites, or whatever premium exists is absorbed by the variance level (control gate) or by SPY/sector-factor exposure (neutralization gate). The mechanism class is thereby narrowed - higher-moment pricing fails at composite level - and no window, band or book tweak may be proposed to rescue it; a reject is terminal for this family in V4 and counts once in the historical denominator.

source_to_test_map.1: Ang-Chen-Xing downside-risk premium + Harvey-Siddique skewness premium + Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw lottery overpricing -> joint implication: long downside-heavy, short upside-heavy, market-neutral spread has positive expectancy -> implemented as the semivariance-share rank of the anchor
source_to_test_map.2: shape (composition) not level is the priced object -> state variable S_i = downside second moment / total second moment over trailing 126 sessions -> anchor step (2)
source_to_test_map.3: premium should attach to persistent risk states, not to shock responses (shock reversal is a forbidden, separately rejected family) -> 126-session smoothed state with monthly ticks and hysteresis entry/exit bands -> anchor step (3)
source_to_test_map.4: market/sector beta must not be mistaken for alpha -> net ~0 book + frozen kappa_t risk-matched SPY-context subtraction + [SPY, EW_SECTOR] intercept neutralization -> factor_alpha_test
source_to_test_map.5: if the mechanism is shape, variance level alone must not carry the spread -> level-sort control with preregistered 0.5 alpha-ratio and expectancy <= 0 falsification rule -> causal_negative_control
source_to_test_map.6: mechanism robustness across state horizons -> 63-session-window neighbour must carry the same sign -> neighbour
source_to_test_map.7: survival after costs -> turnover bounded by hysteresis on a persistent state; base and 20 bps stress reruns -> costs_and_turnover

implementation_estimate.engineer_days: ~2.5 days: signal module (0.5), hysteresis automaton and bookkeeping (1.0), control and neighbour arm configs (0.25), risk-match/sector-neutralization reporting (0.5), fold force-flat harness integration (0.25)
implementation_estimate.risk_notes: automaton determinism is the main risk: transition ordering, capacity checks and lexicographic tie-breaks must be byte-stable; XLC availability edge (eligible only with full 126-session history); automaton re-seed at fold starts must respect force-flat boundaries; kappa_t trailing regression must use data through t-1 only (no leakage); all estimates here are analytic expectations, no PnL computed at proposal time

outcome_blind_attestation: I did not read per-arm V2/V3 outcomes; this proposal was written before any V4 scoring - A4
